subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit LaunchAgent/inherited `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=0` or unset value override OpenClaw-generated durable service env/config values that still contain `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=1`, or should the durable source remain authoritative with a documented doctor/removal path?
rationale: This controls a sensitive logging boundary and may alter service-env precedence for existing operators, so automation should not choose the policy silently.

options.title: Explicit disable wins
options.body: Treat `0`, `false`, `off`, `no`, and unset as an operator disable that prevents generated LaunchAgent env-file raw-stream values from re-enabling logging, with docs and tests for the precedence.

options.title: Durable source wins
options.body: Keep `.env`/config service env as authoritative and update docs/doctor to tell operators to remove or repair that durable source before restart.

options.title: Docs-only for now
options.body: Clarify the current behavior without changing runtime precedence, accepting that launchctl `0` may not stop logging when a generated env file still enables it.

recommendation.title: Explicit disable wins
recommendation.body: Treat `0`, `false`, `off`, `no`, and unset as an operator disable that prevents generated LaunchAgent env-file raw-stream values from re-enabling logging, with docs and tests for the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to both the raw-stream helper migration and daemon/service-env planning history.
